title: Offline image verification, staged rollout, and operator rollback contract
creator: Avery Chen
description: This ticket defines the product requirements and acceptance criteria for performing secure, auditable OS/container image and operator upgrades in Private/VPC (air-gapped or minimal-egress) deployments. The focus is on: verifying artifact provenance offline, enabling staged canary rollouts without internet egress, ensuring deterministic rollback via the operator, and providing physical-media fallback and runbooks for customers with strict no-egress policies.
goals: Provide a deterministic offline image verification process that enforces signature provenance before any upgrade step executes
Define a staged rollout contract (canary -> limited -> full) that is compatible with air-gapped and minimal-egress environments
Ensure operator can perform safe automatic rollback within defined SLOs when upgrade verification or canary health checks fail
Document and validate a physical-media fallback and verification path for customers that disallow network-based sync
non_goals: Building a new artifact distribution service — we will leverage existing registry+mirror mechanisms
Support for arbitrary third-party image formats beyond OCI/tarball signatures at this stage
Replacing customer-side KMS/HSM implementations — we will integrate with them via documented contracts
requirements: Preflight: an agent/cli that runs in-customer environment to validate network rules, registry access (local mirror), and operator version before attempting upgrade
Artifact signing: all images and operator bundles must include a chain of provenance (signer identity, build metadata, checksum) verifiable offline using customer KMS or provided public keys
Signature verification must be enforced by the operator — operator refuses to apply unsigned or unverifiable artifacts
Staged rollout plan must be configurable with explicit sizes and success thresholds (default: 1% canary, 10% limited, 100% full) and a per-stage timeout

Rollback contract: operator must capture pre-upgrade state snapshot (manifest + KV pointers) and be able to revert to that snapshot within 30 minutes of detected regression for clusters up to 50 nodes
Offline sync: support rsync/scp of signed artifact bundles into a local registry mirror and provide a checksum-based acceptance flow
Physical media fallback: documented process for verifying signed bundles from USB/physical media including signature validation steps and integrity checks
KMS rotation compatibility: upgrades must tolerate KMS public-key rotation events when key rollovers are published alongside artifact bundles
Pre-upgrade simulation mode: a dry-run that runs all verification steps and simulates rollout decisions without changing cluster state
Operator safe-mode: operator exposes a safe-mode API to pause rollouts and accept manual approvals during maintenance windows
acceptance_criteria: Automated preflight returns PASS when a cluster has network rules and local mirror reachable; in all other cases it returns an actionable FAIL with remediation steps
Operator rejects any upgrade where artifact signature chain cannot be verified offline using provided key material

Staged canary: in an isolated test cluster that mimics customer constraints (no egress), a full canary-to-full rollout following the contract completes with success thresholds met for 3 consecutive runs
Rollback verified: intentionally induce a canary regression and validate operator rollback completes to the pre-upgrade manifest within 30 minutes for a 20-node test cluster
Physical media test: import an upgrade bundle from a USB disk, verify signatures, perform staged rollout — documented runbook executed by SRE completes without external network access
KMS rotation: simulate a public-key rollover scenario and validate that previously signed artifacts remain verifiable when rollover metadata is supplied alongside the bundle
Preflight and dry-run logs are retained in the console and downloadable as an artifact for audit for at least 90 days
All failure paths produce clear telemetry: reason, failing step, suggested remediation, and a link to runbook; these are surfaced in the Console and in operator logs
Security review signoff obtained and threat-model mitigations documented before release
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design & Spec): finalize signature format and operator verification hooks (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Implementation - Eng): add offline signature verification and preflight checks to operator; implement dry-run mode (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (QA & Test Harness): create air-gapped test harness, physical-media test lab, and run multi-cluster canary tests (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Documentation & Runbooks): publish customer runbooks for rsync/import, USB import, and KMS rollover procedures (1 week)
Phase 4 (Canary Release): enable feature behind feature-flag for opt-in customers; run limited customers in cooperation with Solutions Eng (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (General Availability): promote to GA and update Private deployment contracts and onboarding checklists
test_plan: Unit tests for signature verification logic and operator refusal paths
Integration tests: operator + local registry mirror + KMS simulator in a network-partitioned environment
Chaos tests: simulated partial upgrade and node-level partitioning during canary and rollback
Manual acceptance tests: SRE executes USB-imported bundle upgrade following runbook against an air-gapped cluster
Performance tests: measure time-to-rollback for clusters of sizes 5/20/50 nodes and verify within SLA
Audit tests: confirm that preflight/dry-run logs are recorded and retrievable via console API
risks: Complexity of supporting customer-specific KMS/HSM setups may require additional adapters — could add scope and delay
Customers may have nonstandard local registry setups; robust acceptance and diagnostics are critical to avoid failed upgrades
Physical media introduces supply-chain risks — need strict verification and documented chain-of-custody guidance
Rollback in large clusters may exceed time SLOs under heavy KV/state sizes; require operator optimization or cutover throttles
mitigations_and_decisions: Decision: adopt standard SPDX-like metadata + COSE/PKCS7 for signatures to maximize interoperability
Mitigation: provide an adapter interface for common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, customer HSM via PKCS#11)
Mitigation: implement progressive state snapshotting (shallow manifests then deep KV snapshots) to reduce rollback time
Decision: require signed 'upgrade manifest' that lists contained artifacts and signer identity; operator will refuse upgrades without manifest
stakeholders: Engineering leads: Priya Kapoor (runtime), Marcus Liu (operator), Elena Petrova (infra)
